1: # Vantage-ARS
2: 
3: The public website and founder-controlled, AI-staffed office for Vantage-ARS
4: ([vantage-ars.co.za](https://vantage-ars.co.za)): VoIP, networking and IT
5: infrastructure support, South Africa.
6: 
7: Author: Juan-louw Greyling <juanlouw.greyling@gmail.com>
8: 
9: ## Stack
10: 
11: - TanStack Start + React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Vite 8, Nitro 3
12: - Postgres: Neon (or any Postgres) when `DATABASE_URL` is set, otherwise embedded PGLite
13: - Better Auth (founder email and password), pdf-lib for quotes, Gmail SMTP for notices
14: - Ten AI staff, each with a fixed role, working a durable queue on their own cadence
15: - Nine productised services at published prices; eight can be sold and delivered unattended under a standing founder delegation (ART-13), while the engineer-delivered support plan remains human-gated
16: 
17: ## What is in it
18: 
19: | Area                | Routes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
20: | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
21: | Public site         | `/`, `/services`, `/services/voip`, `/services/networking`, `/services/it-infrastructure`, `/services/ai-automation`, `/services/managed-support`, `/services/cloud-email`, `/services/security`, `/services/backup-recovery`, `/find`, `/assess`, `/automation`, `/guides`, `/rates`, `/work`, `/support`, `/status`, `/terms`, `/privacy` |
22: | Customer quote link | `/q/<token>`: view, download PDF, accept or decline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
23: | Founder office      | `/office`: command, autonomy, approvals, sales, ledger, customer book, site signals, chat, audit, metrics and more                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
24: | Founder governance  | `/office/delegations` (standing delegation), `/office/governance` (rulings, section 71 gates, signed receipts), `/office/revenue` (subscriptions, billing, customer mail), `/office/customers` (the customer book)                                                                                                                          |
25: | Operations          | `/status` (public readiness), `/api/health` (liveness), `/api/cron/floor` (scheduled run), `/api/ai/status`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
26: 
27: ## The office runs itself
28: 
29: With `AUTONOMY=on` and a `CRON_SECRET`, ten agents work a durable queue every
30: ten minutes. Each has named duties on their own cadence: reception classifies
31: enquiries, marketing scores leads on what the buyer actually wrote, flags repeat
32: site interest as prospects, and drafts weekly owned-channel campaigns, then files
33: a founder-gated handoff when demand is real; sales drafts real follow-ups on real
34: quotes, the service desk drafts acknowledgements, technical writes procedures,
35: finance chases overdue invoices, bills the subscriptions that are due and duns
36: the ones that are not, admin checks the filing and reviews the recurring-revenue
37: book, the orchestrator briefs you once a day from the books, and compliance halts
38: the office if the audit chain ever fails to verify. It also reminds the founder
39: weekly when an approval has waited a week; it never approves one on a timer.
40: 
41: None of them email a customer, spend money, win or lose a customer, or publish
42: anything. Those are founder approvals, with the constitutional trace attached —
43: unless you have granted a standing delegation.
44: 
45: Full detail, including every duty and every brake: **[docs/autonomy.md](docs/autonomy.md)**.
46: 
47: ## Standing delegation (ART-13)
48: 
49: Nothing is delegated by default. The office ships with no delegation at all, and
50: it stops at the founder gate for every cost, every customer win, every customer
51: loss and every marketing-to-sales handoff.
52: 
53: A delegation is the founder answering a whole class of question in advance:
54: "for this bounded class of action, at this price, up to this many times a day,
55: you may act without asking me again." It names the action kinds it covers, the
56: published rate lines it may charge, the most any single action may be worth, and
57: how many actions it may take per day and per month. It is revocable, and
58: revocation takes effect on the very next action.
59: 
60: A delegation never overrides a hard block. It cannot widen an agent's role,
61: permit a price that is not published, permit a promise to a customer, or survive
62: a halt. Every action taken under one is written into the audit chain against the
63: delegation that allowed it.
64: 
65: The founder sets it at **`/office/delegations`**. Four presets are offered, and
66: none of them is on until it is saved.
67: 
68: ## Productised services and recurring revenue
69: 
70: Nine services are published with a fixed scope, a fixed price and a
71: deliverable the office can produce from its own records: the managed support
72: plan and the remote health and spend watch, both monthly; the quarterly
73: infrastructure review; and the service report, the billing and rate compliance
74: audit, the infrastructure documentation and handover pack, the business
75: continuity plan, the service level and response review and the fault pattern
76: and incident review, all one-off.
77: 
78: Because the office can deliver them and can bill them, they are recurring
79: revenue rather than jobs. A subscription bills on its own cycle, the
80: deliverable is compiled from the office's own records, and the customer is sent
81: their report and their invoice. Every email the office sends is kept in full
82: under `customer_notices`.
83: 
84: None of it happens on its own. The office delivers and bills a plan only under
85: a delegation, and emails a customer only under a delegation that allows mail.
86: The book is at **`/office/revenue`**; the plans and their prices are on
87: **`/rates`** and **`/services/managed-support`**.
88: 
89: The customer book at **`/office/customers`** assembles every company the office
90: has actually touched — enquiry, lead, opportunity, invoice, receipt and
91: subscription — into one account with its status, open balance and monthly value.
92: It exports the book as CSV. It does not invent a customer from a page view.
93: 
94: Autonomous quoting, subscription start, recurring billing and fulfilment are
95: limited to plans the office can deliver from its own records without human
96: labour. The managed support plan includes engineer hours, so it is not sold or
97: billed unattended even if a delegation includes its rate.
98: 
99: Support time is logged at **`/office/service`** against the account, with the
100: minutes, a note and the work date. A service report uses that recorded time when
101: it exists and falls back to the one-hour-per-fault estimate, labelled as an
102: estimate, when it does not. The ledger journal and the combined audit/decision
103: chain also export as formula-safe CSV.
104: 
105: The governance record at **`/office/governance`** brings together the founder's
106: precedent rulings, section 71 gate records and signed execution receipts. Each
107: receipt signature is checked at read time; an approval that was skipped stays
108: visibly undecided at the gate. Ctrl/⌘ K opens office-wide search across the
109: founder snapshot — customers, approvals, tickets, money records, decisions and
110: pages — without exposing a public index.
111: 
112: **`/find`** asks three plain questions — the problem, the impact and the horizon
113: — and recommends a published service, the guides that explain it and a short
114: checklist before an enquiry. It recommends; it does not quote or promise an
115: outcome.
116: 
117: **`/assess`** is a browser-only IT readiness self-assessment across seven
118: operational practices. It separates unknowns from answers a visitor can assess,
119: and links improvement areas to existing service lines. It is not a technical
120: audit, security test or compliance certification; answers are not submitted or
121: saved unless the visitor explicitly attaches a short summary to a quote request.
122: That request offers the published initial remote assessment (up to 60 minutes);
123: scope and VAT treatment are confirmed in writing before any work starts.
124: 
125: **`/automation`** is a browser-only workflow planning checklist. It considers
126: repeat frequency, process clarity, information quality, known exceptions,
127: impact of errors and human approval controls, then distinguishes a bounded
128: pilot candidate from workflows that need controls first. The result is
129: deterministic, not AI-generated advice. Visitors can copy or download a local
130: pilot brief, or explicitly attach it to a written-scope quote request; it is not
131: sent unless the visitor submits the enquiry.
132: 
133: **`/services/ai-automation`** describes five human-led engagements: workflow
134: readiness review, agent blueprint, supervised workflow pilot, read-only
135: diagnostics pilot and governance/operations pack. Every engagement is scoped
136: and quoted using applicable published labour rates; model and software fees
137: remain separate. Diagnostics use customer-authorized read-only data;
138: production access, system scans, unattended actions and ongoing monitoring are
139: not included by default.
140: 
141: Marketing at **`/office/marketing`** also shows the last thirty days of real
142: site signals: page views by day, top pages, referral sources, countries and the
143: latest events. The record holds no IP address, no cookie and no inferred
144: identity; anonymous site signals are not a cold-contact list. Paid campaign
145: proposals are capped at R300 per Johannesburg calendar month, still require
146: founder approval, and cannot launch ads until an advertising account is
147: connected.
148: 
149: ## Run locally
150: 
151: Node 22.12 or newer.
152: 
153: ```sh
154: npm ci
155: cp .env.example .env      # fill in what you need; everything is optional locally
156: npm run dev               # http://localhost:8080
157: npm run validate          # typecheck + lint + tests
158: npm run verify:office     # boots a real office and proves it runs autonomously
159: ```
160: 
161: `npm run verify:office` is the one that matters. It starts a real embedded
162: Postgres, files the records the public site would really file, runs the real
163: scheduler, and asserts on what the real agents did — 243 checks, no mocks and
164: no sample data. If autonomy breaks, this fails.
165: 
166: ## Environment
167: 
168: Everything is in [`.env.example`](.env.example). The ones that matter:
169: 
170: | Variable                                                            | Purpose                                                                              |
171: | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
172: | `DATABASE_URL`                                                      | Postgres (Neon). Migrations run during `npm run build`. Unset means embedded PGLite. |
173: | `PGLITE_DATA_DIR`                                                   | With PGLite, keep data here. Unset means in-memory, lost on restart.                 |
174: | `BETTER_AUTH_URL`                                                   | The public URL.                                                                      |
175: | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`                                                | A long random secret (`openssl rand -base64 32`). Required in production.            |
176: | `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN`                                               | One-time code for creating the founder account. Remove it afterwards.                |
177: | `FOUNDER_EMAIL`                                                     | The only account allowed into the office.                                            |
178: | `AUTONOMY`                                                          | `on` lets the office act unattended. Anything else and only the button works.        |
179: | `CRON_SECRET`                                                       | Bearer token the scheduler must present. 16+ characters.                             |
180: | `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_FROM` | Optional outbound mail over implicit TLS (port 465); use a provider-verified sender. |
181: | `GMAIL_SMTP_USER`, `GMAIL_SMTP_APP_PASSWORD`                        | Legacy Gmail fallback; messages use the Gmail account as sender.                     |
182: | `FOUNDER_WEBHOOK_URL`                                               | Optional HTTPS webhook for the same founder notices (Slack, Discord or generic).     |
183: | `PAYMENT_*`                                                         | Bank details on the site and quotes.                                                 |
184: | `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` / `XAI_API_KEY`     | AI staff reasoning. Every autonomous duty works without it.                          |
185: 
186: Nothing new is needed for the delegation or the productised services. A
187: delegation is set inside the office. Generic SMTP supports a verified
188: `hello@vantage-ars.co.za` sender; the legacy Gmail fallback continues to send
189: from the configured Gmail account. Set up the provider mailbox and publish its
190: SPF/DKIM records before switching the sender.
191: 
192: ## Founder setup (once)
193: 
194: 1. Set `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN` and, if needed, `FOUNDER_EMAIL`. Deploy.
195: 2. Open `/office`. The page offers "First-time founder setup".
196: 3. Enter the founder email, a password of 12+ characters and the setup token.
197: 4. Remove `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN` and redeploy. Sign-up is closed once a founder exists.
198: 
199: ## Final launch verification
200: 
201: Before you brand the project live, run the final launch gate:
202: 
203: ```sh
204: npm run final:check
205: ```
206: 
207: This enforces the production deployment checks and then runs the repo-wide
208: verification pass (`typecheck`, lint and the real office tests). It is the
209: single final gate before pushing to production.
210: 
211: ## Next steps
212: 
213: The execution roadmap for turning this into a live, revenue-generating operation is in
214: [docs/next-steps.md](docs/next-steps.md). It covers launch, monitoring,
215: research/AI expansion, marketing, recurring revenue, and the governance guardrails that keep the office safe.
216: 
217: ## Deploy
218: 
219: **[docs/deploy-vercel.md](docs/deploy-vercel.md) is the full walkthrough** — the
220: variables to set, the founder setup, the domain cutover, and how to verify it.
221: 
222: ### Vercel + Neon (recommended)
223: 
224: 1. Import the GitHub repo in Vercel.
225: 2. Add a Neon database and set `DATABASE_URL`, then the auth settings above.
226: 3. Set `AUTONOMY=on` and a generated `CRON_SECRET`. The ten-minute tick is
227:    scheduled by the `office-scheduler` GitHub Actions workflow — add the same
228:    `CRON_SECRET` as a repository secret (Settings → Secrets and variables →
229:    Actions) so the scheduler call authenticates. GitHub's cron is best-effort
230:    on quiet repositories, so the office also nudges itself: a hit on
231:    `/api/health` or a real page view starts a catch-up tick when the last one
232:    is over ten minutes old. `vercel.json` keeps a daily run as the final
233:    fallback (Vercel's Hobby plan rejects crons more often than daily).
234: 4. Deploy. `npm run build` applies migrations.
235: 5. Check `https://www.vantage-ars.co.za/api/health` — `scheduler.overdue` should
236:    be `false`.
237: 
238: ### Docker (any server)
239: 
240: ```sh
241: cp .env.example .env      # set AUTONOMY=on, CRON_SECRET, auth settings
242: docker compose up -d --build
243: ```
244: 
245: The compose file also starts a `scheduler` sidecar that ticks
246: `/api/cron/floor` every ten minutes with your `CRON_SECRET`, so an unattended
247: server never depends on GitHub Actions cron.
248: 
249: ### Plain Node
250: 
251: ```sh
252: npm ci && npm run build && npm start      # .output/server/index.mjs, PORT defaults to 3000
253: ```
254: 
255: For an always-on server without Docker, `deploy/systemd/` ships a service unit
256: plus a timer that ticks the floor every ten minutes.
257: 
258: ## Operations
259: 
260: **Health.** `GET /api/health` answers "is the business running?" — database,
261: audit chain, scheduler freshness, work queue, mail delivery, and the money
262: position. It returns 503 when something that matters is wrong, and never exposes
263: a secret or a customer. Sign in and it returns the full picture. Hitting it also
264: nudges a stale scheduler back on cadence, so an uptime monitor doubles as the
265: heartbeat.
266: 
267: **Public status.** `/status` is a readiness check, not an uptime page: five
268: lines read from the office at the moment it loads — records, decision-record
269: integrity, scheduled work, published-rate agreement and founder control. The
270: full health document is reduced on the server, so money, customers, the halt
271: reason and delegation limits never reach a visitor. It keeps no history and
272: makes no availability promise.
273: 
274: **Autonomy UI.** `/office` shows the scheduler state, every duty and when it is
275: next due, the live queue, and what each agent did last. The same panel runs the
276: office on demand through the identical code path. It also lists the
277: dead-letter queue on its own, with the error that killed each item, and lets
278: the founder redrive one: redriving is a founder action, never an automatic one,
279: and it is written to the audit chain.
280: 
281: **Money.** Amounts are integer cents. A receipt may only retire money actually
282: owed — the balance update and the ledger row are one transaction that reads the
283: receivable under lock. A quote's figure is generated from the published rate
284: card, never from agent prose.
285: 
286: **Audit chain.** Every decision and every event is hash-chained in one
287: transaction under an advisory lock, so the chain cannot fork. SEAL verifies the
288: whole chain twice a day and halts the office if it fails. `/office/audit` shows
289: the result.
290: 
291: **Backup.** `/office/audit` exports every business table as JSON with a SHA-256
292: checksum, including live customer quote links. Restore is add-only and
293: transactional: it never deletes or overwrites, and a half-restored office is
294: impossible.
295: 
296: ## CI
297: 
298: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs typecheck, lint, tests, a production build and
299: the office verification on every push to `main` and every pull request.
300: 
301: ## Docs
302: 
303: - [docs/autonomy.md](docs/autonomy.md): every duty, every brake, and why.
304: - [docs/autonomy-runbook.md](docs/autonomy-runbook.md): the switches that make the office run itself, per deploy target.
305: - [docs/autonomy-roadmap.md](docs/autonomy-roadmap.md): what is verified running today, and the ordered increments to a fully unattended office.
306: - [docs/governance-architecture.md](docs/governance-architecture.md): the five planes, the risk tiers, the dead-letter queue, and what is deliberately not implemented.
307: - [docs/deploy-vercel.md](docs/deploy-vercel.md): environment, cutover, verification.
308: - [docs/business-scope-and-competitive-pricing.md](docs/business-scope-and-competitive-pricing.md): scope, rates and department boundaries.
309: - [docs/cloudflare-workers-ai.md](docs/cloudflare-workers-ai.md): account id, API token, per-host env, verification.
310: - [docs/MERGE.md](docs/MERGE.md): how the earlier projects were combined.
311: - [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed and when.
312: 
313: ## Governance
314: 
315: Agents act only inside their role. Anything that costs money, risks a customer,
316: or can win one goes to the founder for approval, unless a standing delegation
317: covers it. Every decision is recorded in a hash-chained audit trail that the
318: office verifies on its own.
319: 
320: The founder's own rulings are recorded too, and in more detail than the chain

1: # The autonomous office
2: 
3: This is how Vantage-ARS runs itself, and — more importantly — what stops it
4: doing anything it must not.
5: 
6: ## The idea
7: 
8: The office is ten agents with fixed roles and no memory. It does not "decide to
9: be busy". Instead it keeps its own to-do list in Postgres, and a scheduler that
10: runs every ten minutes asks each agent a single question: **given what is
11: actually on the books, is there a real thing worth doing?**
12: 
13: An empty answer is a successful run. Most of the time, the honest answer is that
14: nothing needed doing, and the office says so rather than manufacturing activity.
15: 
16: ## The pace
17: 
18: The office does not run every tick at the same width. It reads the state it is
19: about to work on and chooses a posture: `idle`, `steady`, `surge` or `recovery`.
20: The posture sets how many items each agent may run, how many the tick may run in
21: total, and whether customer-response duties may run at half their normal
22: cadence. It never widens what an agent is allowed to do — the governor still
23: sits in front of every action.
24: 
25: | Posture  | Per agent | Per tick | Response cadence | Chosen when                                                                                          |
26: | -------- | --------- | -------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
27: | idle     | 4         | 24       | normal           | nothing is waiting                                                                                   |
28: | steady   | 8         | 48       | normal           | ordinary queued or due work                                                                          |
29: | surge    | 12        | 72       | half, floor 5m   | a live P0/P1 ticket, a customer waiting, an undelivered billed period, or a queue of 12 open / 8 due |
30: | recovery | 3         | 18       | normal           | three consecutive failing ticks, or the tick that clears the circuit breaker                         |
31: 
32: A "customer waiting" is an unanswered inbound item older than thirty minutes or
33: a chat older than twenty. An "undelivered billed period" is a period the office
34: has invoiced but not yet delivered. These are facts from the office's own
35: tables, not a target the scheduler invents. During a surge only duties that
36: answer or deliver to a customer are accelerated: `foyer_intake`,
37: `close_win_handoff`, `close_quote_notice`, `desk_acknowledge`,
38: `desk_sla_watch`, `desk_chat_reply`, `desk_service_fulfilment`,
39: `desk_service_notice`, `ledger_payment_notices` and
40: `ledger_subscription_billing`.
41: 
42: The budgets are per tick, not per day. The per-agent cap stops one agent from
43: draining the whole tick; the total cap stops the tick from running until the
44: timer fires again. Both are recorded with the posture on `office_state`, so the
45: founder's autonomy panel shows the pace the scheduler actually chose rather than
46: reconstructing it from the queue afterwards.
47: 
48: ```
49:                  ┌──────────────┐
50:    GET           │  /api/cron   │  Bearer CRON_SECRET, AUTONOMY=on
51:    /api/cron ───▶│    /floor    │  every 10 minutes
52:    /floor        └──────┬───────┘
53:                         │
54:                  ┌──────▼───────┐
55:                  │  refuse to   │  halted?  DB down?  chain broken?
56:                  │  run blind   │  5 failing ticks in a row?
57:                  └──────┬───────┘
58:                         │  no
59:                  ┌──────▼───────────┐
60:       38 duties → │      PLAN        │  pure function of the real office state
61:                  └──────┬───────────┘  returns work, or nothing
62:                         │
63:                  ┌──────▼───────────┐
64:                  │  work_items      │  deduped by a partial unique index
65:                  │  (the queue)     │  claimed atomically, backoff on failure
66:                  └──────┬───────────┘
67:                         │
68:                  ┌──────▼───────────┐
69:                  │      EXECUTE     │  every action through the governor
70:                  └──────┬───────────┘
71:                         │
72:                  ┌──────▼───────────┐
73:                  │  audit chain     │  one transaction, one lock, one head
74:                  └──────────────────┘
75: ```
76: 
77: ## The duties
78: 
79: Thirty-eight duties, every agent has at least one, and none of them can act
80: outside its owner's role.
81: 
82: | Agent   | Duty                          | Cadence | What it does with real records                                                                                                                                                                               |
83: | ------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
84: | VANTAGE | `vantage_liveness`            | 30m     | Reports an agent that has work waiting and is not working, or has never run                                                                                                                                  |
85: | VANTAGE | `vantage_backlog`             | 60m     | Reports a stuck queue and anything abandoned after retries                                                                                                                                                   |
86: | VANTAGE | `vantage_briefing`            | 24h     | One factual daily summary for the founder: books, pipeline, queue, last day's activity — every figure from a record                                                                                          |
87: | VANTAGE | `vantage_approval_watch`      | 168h    | Reminds the founder weekly about approvals pending for seven days; links to the approval desk and never resolves them                                                                                        |
88: | FOYER   | `foyer_intake`                | 10m     | Classifies unrouted enquiries into a lead or a service ticket                                                                                                                                                |
89: | FOYER   | `foyer_stale_intake`          | 60m     | Escalates an enquiry nobody answered after four hours                                                                                                                                                        |
90: | SIGNAL  | `signal_site_signals`         | 12h     | Reads real recorded page views and says what they mean                                                                                                                                                       |
91: | SIGNAL  | `signal_content_brief`        | 24h     | Briefs the next owned-site piece, or names pages with no traffic                                                                                                                                             |
92: | SIGNAL  | `signal_draft_campaign`       | 168h    | Drafts one owned-channel campaign per week for nurtured leads not yet in sales. Activation is a founder approval; paid campaigns are hard-capped at R300 per Johannesburg calendar month.                    |
93: | SIGNAL  | `signal_prospect`             | 24h     | Flags repeat visits to buying pages as a `Prospect ·` lead. No contact is invented.                                                                                                                          |
94: | SIGNAL  | `signal_qualify_leads`        | 3h      | Scores every lead on what the buyer actually wrote                                                                                                                                                           |
95: | SIGNAL  | `signal_handoff`              | 2h      | Files a founder-gated sales handoff for genuine buying intent                                                                                                                                                |
96: | CLOSE   | `close_discovery`             | 4h      | Opens a qualified lead that came in through a real channel, and writes a discovery checklist against a live opportunity                                                                                      |
97: | CLOSE   | `close_quote`                 | 60m     | Issues a published-rate quote for a real enquiry when a delegation covers quoting. Human-delivered plans are held for the founder; the line comes from the quote playbook, never from the model.              |
98: | CLOSE   | `close_quote_followup`        | 12h     | Drafts a follow-up once a real quote has waited two days                                                                                                                                                     |
99: | CLOSE   | `close_stale_proposal`        | 24h     | Reports a proposal with no movement for fourteen days                                                                                                                                                        |
100: | CLOSE   | `close_win_handoff`           | 60m     | Flags a won deal with delivery open and no invoice                                                                                                                                                           |
101: | CLOSE   | `close_quote_notice`          | 2h      | Emails approved quotes and sends an approved, scope-specific observation checklist after an accepted diagnostic quote. Customer mail requires an active email delegation.                                    |
102: | DESK    | `desk_acknowledge`            | 30m     | Drafts an acknowledgement for an unanswered service request                                                                                                                                                  |
103: | DESK    | `desk_sla_watch`              | 2h      | Escalates tickets past their severity's time limit                                                                                                                                                           |
104: | DESK    | `desk_chat_reply`             | 15m     | Drafts a reply to a chat that has been waiting                                                                                                                                                               |
105: | DESK    | `desk_service_fulfilment`     | 60m     | Produces the deliverable for an invoiced period from the office's own records and files it as a document. The agent never writes it.                                                                         |
106: | DESK    | `desk_service_notice`         | 60m     | Emails the customer the report for a delivered period, from the office's own template, to an address already on file                                                                                         |
107: | FORGE   | `forge_diagnose`              | 30m     | Writes a procedure against an open fault. Never marks it fixed                                                                                                                                               |
108: | FORGE   | `forge_knowledge`             | 24h     | Turns a resolved fault's procedure into knowledge-base text                                                                                                                                                  |
109: | LEDGER  | `ledger_chase_invoice`        | 24h     | Drafts a reminder for an invoice unpaid after seven days                                                                                                                                                     |
110: | LEDGER  | `ledger_payment_notices`      | 2h      | Matches a payment notice to an invoice to the cent and books the receipt, or puts the notice in front of the founder                                                                                         |
111: | LEDGER  | `ledger_payables`             | 24h     | Reports money owed out, for the founder to schedule                                                                                                                                                          |
112: | LEDGER  | `ledger_start_subscription`   | 4h      | Starts an eligible record-based plan the customer bought: a won opportunity with an accepted quote and no subscription yet                                                                                   |
113: | LEDGER  | `ledger_subscription_billing` | 60m     | Invoices eligible record-based subscriptions whose own billing date has passed, using the period the subscription says                                                                                      |
114: | LEDGER  | `ledger_dunning`              | 4h      | Reminds a customer about an invoice open for seven days or more, and only while a delegation allows it. After nine weeks the office stops emailing about it and the invoice is left to the founder.          |
115: | LEDGER  | `ledger_billing`              | 30m     | Invoices accepted work from the quoted figure under billing delegation. Diagnostic quotes wait until their linked delivery ticket is resolved; invoices and receipts are emailed only under mail delegation. |
116: | KEEP    | `keep_records`                | 12h     | Reports a won deal with no quote, invoice or receipt filed                                                                                                                                                   |
117: | KEEP    | `keep_subscription_review`    | 168h    | Reviews the recurring-revenue book weekly: subscriptions past their billing date, and whether the published prices still match the plans the office sells                                                    |
118: | SEAL    | `seal_chain_verify`           | 12h     | **Halts the office** if the audit chain does not verify                                                                                                                                                      |
119: | SEAL    | `seal_scope_audit`            | 24h     | Reports escalations that suggest an agent is unsure of its role                                                                                                                                              |
120: 
121: ## What autonomy is allowed to do
122: 
123: Every duty action goes through the same constitutional governor as a manual
124: dispatch. Without a delegation in place, the standing boundary is the one the
125: office has always had:
126: 
127: **Agents may** — file leads, open tickets, write drafts, advance records the
128: founder has already authorised, score, and file internal briefs.
129: 
130: **Agents may not** — email a customer, spend money, win or lose a customer, issue
131: an invoice, or publish anything. Each of those is an escalation, and every
132: escalation is a founder approval with the constitutional trace attached.
133: 
134: That is the default, and the office ships with it. ART-13 lets the founder
135: change it once, in advance, for a bounded class of work. A delegation is the
136: founder writing down: "for these action kinds, at these published prices, up to
137: this much for any single action and this many times a day and a month, you may
138: act and bill without asking me again."
139: 
140: Inside that envelope the office acts and bills on its own. Outside it, nothing
141: changes: the same gate, the same escalation, the same constitutional trace.
142: 
143: Five things stay impossible, delegation or no delegation:
144: 
145: 1. **Emailing a customer without a delegation that allows it.**
146:    `send_customer_mail` is one of only four action kinds that exist solely under
147:    a delegation, and the policy must both list it and set the customer-mail
148:    flag. The body is rendered from a template written in `customer-mail.ts`; an
149:    agent never supplies the wording. The rendered body is checked once more
150:    before it is allowed out, and a body containing a promise word — guarantee,
151:    uptime, 24/7, SLA, fixed price, discount, free — is not sent at all. Without
152:    a delegation, customer letters are drafted, never sent.
153: 2. **Charging anyone without an accepted quote or a won job.** `issue_invoice`,
154:    `record_inbound_payment` and `start_subscription` are money actions, and each
155:    is refused unless the customer has an accepted quote on file or a won
156:    opportunity. A delegation may demand that of every action it covers. The
157:    check reads the whole table, never a window.
158: 3. **Quoting a price that is not on the published card.** The governor re-prices
159:    the quote from the published rate and refuses any amount that does not match
160:    it. A delegation may only name rate lines that exist and are offered; a
161:    withheld line can never be delegated, and the office checks weekly that the
162:    published prices still match the plans it sells.
163: 4. **Selling to a customer who never contacted us.** `open_opportunity`,
164:    `issue_quote` and `propose_close_won` need a real enquiry — a row in the
165:    inbound log for that company name. A lead the office invented from a page
166:    view has none, and no delegation reaches it.
167: 5. **Approving an unanswered approval on a timer.** An escalation is resolved
168:    by the founder, in the office, one decision at a time. Nothing expires an
169:    approval into a decision, and no delegation creates one.
170: 
171: ## Delegated authority (ART-13)
172: 
173: ART-13 is the one article that lets the founder satisfy the founder gate once,
174: in advance, for a class of action instead of once per action. A delegation is
175: deliberately boring. It names:
176: 
177: - the action kinds it covers, from a closed list of nine — `open_opportunity`,
178:   `issue_quote`, `propose_close_won`, `issue_invoice`,
179:   `record_inbound_payment`, `start_subscription`, `cancel_subscription`,
180:   `fulfil_service`, `send_customer_mail`;
181: - the published rate lines it may charge;
182: - the most any single action may be worth;
183: - how many actions it may take per day, and how many per month.
184: 
185: When the founder starts a delegation the defaults are R5,000.00 for a single
186: action, 20 actions a day and 200 a month. The founder may set any of them, and
187: the monthly limit may not be smaller than the daily limit. There is one
188: delegation: it is edited, paused and revoked, never duplicated. It is managed on
189: `/office/delegations`.
190: 
191: **What a delegation can never override.** It does not weaken the constitution. It
192: cannot widen an agent's role, cannot permit a promise to a customer, cannot
193: permit a price that is not published, and cannot survive a halt. The delegation
194: check runs after the absolute blocks, so it can never rescue an action that was
195: already refused for role separation, human dignity, instruction override or
196: non-discrimination reasons. Four action kinds exist only under a delegation —
197: `fulfil_service`, `start_subscription`, `cancel_subscription` and
198: `send_customer_mail` — and without one they are refused rather than escalated.
199: 
200: A founder action is not a delegated action. The delegation is read only for
201: work the office does on its own, so a founder's own action never spends the
202: office's autonomous budget, and the caps always measure autonomous work.
203: 
204: **Revocation takes effect on the very next action.** The policy is read fresh
205: inside the same transaction that performs the action, so a revoked delegation is
206: refused with `revoked` and a paused one with `paused` before anything is
207: written. There is no grace period and no queue of work that was already
208: approved: the next tick sees the change.
209: 
210: **Usage is counted from real rows.** Every action taken under a delegation
211: writes a `delegation_usage` row in the same transaction that took the action,
212: carrying the action kind, the amount, the company and the UTC day and month.
213: The caps are a count over those rows rather than a counter in memory, so a
214: retried tick cannot slip past a cap and a restart cannot reset one.
215: 
216: The office can pause a delegation without ending it, and the presets on
217: `/office/delegations` are four starting points: Observe only, Deliver and tell
218: the customer, Bill and collect, and Managed revenue. None of them is on by
219: default.
220: 
221: ## Recurring revenue
222: 
223: A recurring plan is a quote, an acceptance and a schedule. The office can run
224: the whole loop on its own, once a delegation covers it, only when the full plan
225: can be delivered from office records without human labour. The managed support
226: plan includes eight engineer hours; its quotes, subscription starts, recurring
227: invoices and fulfilment are therefore held out of unattended operation. A
228: delegation cannot turn staff work the office does not perform into an automated
229: deliverable.
230: 
231: 1. **Quote.** The price comes from the published rate card and from nothing
232:    else.
233: 2. **The customer accepts on their link.** The quote reaches the customer as a
234:    link, valid for thirty days. The customer accepts by name on the link. That
235:    one action closes the opportunity as won, marks the quote accepted and opens
236:    the delivery ticket — idempotently, so a double click cannot open two.
237: 3. **The office starts the subscription.** A won opportunity with an accepted
238:    quote for a recurring plan, and no subscription yet, becomes a subscription.
239:    If the price on the quote does not match the published plan price, nothing
240:    is started. The period the customer bought is the first one, and the
241:    subscription recurs from the day that period ends, so nobody is billed
242:    twice for the same month.
243: 4. **The period is invoiced.** When the subscription's own next billing instant
244:    arrives, the billing duty plans one work item for it. The period boundaries
245:    come from the subscription, not from a window the office chose. The invoice
246:    goes through the governor like any other invoice, so the delegation caps and
247:    the money guards apply exactly as they do to a founder-raised invoice.
248: 5. **The deliverable is produced from the office's own records.** The report is
249:    assembled from tickets, quotes, invoices, support time and measured response
250:    times, and filed as a document. When the founder has logged support time for
251:    the period, the report uses it; otherwise it labels the remote-hours figure as
252:    an estimate. The agent asks for the deliverable and the office
253:    produces it; it never writes the customer's text. Where the office holds no
254:    record of something, the report says so rather than filling the gap.
255: 6. **The customer is emailed.** The notice duty sends the report to an address
256:    the office already holds for that customer, rendered from the office's own
257:    template. The notice is written down before the send, and the send happens
258:    after the transaction commits, so a slow mail server cannot hold the audit
259:    lock open. A notice that could not be sent stays on file as `not_delivered`
260:    with the reason.
261: 7. **The payment is matched and the receipt is booked.** The customer files a
262:    payment notice. If it carries a reference on an open invoice and an amount
263:    that matches to the cent, the receipt is booked, the invoice is marked paid
264:    and the period is closed. Anything that does not match exactly goes to the
265:    founder, and treasury does not move.
266: 
267: Which of those steps need a person:
268: 
269: - **Autonomous once the delegation is in place for eligible, record-based plans:** the quote notice, the invoice
270:   for the period, the deliverable, the customer email, the payment reminder,
271:   and the matching of an exact payment to an invoice.
272: - **Still a person's decision:** anything above the delegation's cap, anything
273:   the delegation does not cover, every refund or credit, every concession to a
274:   customer, and every customer win or loss the delegation does not cover. The
275:   office never ends a subscription on its own initiative: no duty plans a
276:   cancellation, and the founder ends one from the office.
277: - **Only possible under a delegation:** every step in the list above. With no
278:   delegation the same flow stops at the founder gate at each step — the quote
279:   is approved by hand, the invoice is raised by hand, the report is produced by
280:   hand, and the email is drafted rather than sent.
281: 
282:   The managed support plan is a separate case: its published scope includes
283:   engineer labour. It is not autonomously quoted, started, billed, or marked
284:   fulfilled, even when a delegation names the rate. A founder can still sell and
285:   manage that plan through the human workflow. Any already-invoiced cycle that
286:   lacks a report or customer notice is surfaced in the recurring-revenue review
287:   for founder attention rather than silently dropped from fulfilment.
288: 
289: ## What stops it
290: 
291: Five independent brakes, any one of which is sufficient:
292: 
293: 1. **Halt.** The founder can halt from the office shell or the API. No duty
294:    plans anything while halted, and a halted office refuses queued approvals.
295: 2. **Database health.** A tick refuses to run if the database is unreachable or
296:    the schema is missing, rather than planning work it cannot record.
297: 3. **The audit chain.** Every tick refuses ordinary work when the chain does not
298:    verify: only SEAL runs, and the seal duty halts the office. SEAL also verifies
299:    the whole hash chain on its twelve-hour cadence, because an office that cannot
300:    prove what it did must not keep acting.
301: 4. **A circuit breaker, with a self-check.** Five consecutive failing ticks and
302:    the scheduler refuses to act. After a thirty-minute cooldown it may make one
303:    clean probe — the real database, the chain and the halt state — and if they
304:    are healthy it clears the breaker, writes `scheduler_recovered` to the audit
305:    chain and resumes at the recovery budget. If the probe is not clean, the
306:    breaker stays closed. Three consecutive failures already slow the office to
307:    the recovery budget before the breaker trips.
308: 5. **The governor.** Role separation, published pricing, dignity,
309:    non-discrimination, confidence floors, and the founder gates on cost, customer
310:    win, customer loss and marketing-to-sales handoff — applied to every single
311:    action, autonomous or not, and satisfied in advance only where a delegation
312:    says so.
313: 
314: ## Idempotency
315: 
316: The scheduler runs on a timer that retries, on multiple serverless instances,
317: can be triggered by hand at the same moment, and is nudged opportunistically
318: when a public surface (a health poll, a page-view beacon) sees that the last
319: tick is more than ten minutes old. Three mechanisms make all of that safe:
320: 
321: - A **partial unique index** on `work_items.dedupe_key where status = 'open'`
322:   means a recurring duty can never stack two open items for the same record. The
323:   database rejects the duplicate, not a check-then-insert race.
324: - Work is **claimed atomically** (`update ... where status = 'open'`), so two
325:   ticks cannot run the same item.
326: - Money guards query the **whole table**, never the windowed snapshot the UI
327:   renders from. The old code checked "is there already an invoice for this
328:   opportunity?" against the 80 most recent ledger rows, so past 80 rows it
329:   stopped protecting the books.
330: 
331: A billing period is invoiced once. The unique index on
332: `(subscription_id, period_start)` and a conditional claim inside the invoice
333: transaction mean that a retried tick, a restarted server and two concurrent
334: ticks cannot bill the same month twice.
335: 
336: `scripts/verify-office.mjs` runs the floor again and again past its own
337: cadences, and asserts that no invoice is booked twice and no quote is
338: duplicated.
339: 
340: ## Money
341: 
342: - Amounts are integer cents throughout. No float arithmetic on money.
343: - A receipt may only retire money that is actually owed. Crediting more than the
344:   outstanding receivable is impossible, because the balance update and the
345:   ledger row happen in one transaction that reads the receivable under lock.
346: - An invoice is bound to won work: a job invoice to a won opportunity, a
347:   recurring invoice to the billing period it covers. A quote's figure is
348:   generated from `QUOTE_SPECS`, never from anything an agent wrote.
349: - A delegated action may only charge a published rate line, and the delegation's
350:   own cap applies on top of it. The office never prices a plan from a figure it
351:   invented: a plan whose published price has drifted from the rate card is
352:   reported, and a subscription whose quoted price does not match the published
353:   plan price is not started.
354: 
355: ## Running it
356: 
357: ```sh
358: AUTONOMY=on CRON_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)   # in the host environment
359: ```
360: 
361: Then either press **Run the floor** on `/office` — the same code path — or wait
362: for the schedule. The schedule alone is not enough: GitHub throttles frequent
363: cron on quiet repositories, so a hit on `/api/health`, the page-view beacon, or
364: the founder loading the floor also starts a catch-up tick when the last one is
365: over ten minutes old. A monitor polling health therefore doubles as the
366: heartbeat. `/api/health` reports whether it is actually running:
367: 
368: ```sh
369: curl -s https://www.vantage-ars.co.za/api/health | jq '.scheduler, .problems'
370: ```
371: 
372: ## Proving it works
373: 
374: ```sh
375: npm run verify:office
376: ```
377: 
378: This boots the real application modules against a real embedded Postgres, files
379: the records the public site would really file, runs the real scheduler, and
380: asserts on what the real agents actually did — 243 checks, no mocks, no
381: fixtures.

content.text:
# Vantage-ARS next steps

This is the execution list for taking the project from a verified, founder-governed office into a live commercial operating system.

## Phase 1 — production launch

1. Set all required production variables on the host.
   - DATABASE_URL
   - BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
   - BETTER_AUTH_URL
   - FOUNDER_EMAIL
   - CRON_SECRET
   - AUTONOMY=on
2. Deploy the app and confirm the health endpoint is reachable.
3. Create the founder account once using FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN.
4. Remove FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN and redeploy.
5. Open /office and save the first standing delegation policy.
6. Verify the office queue and scheduler are active.

## Phase 2 — live operations and monitoring

1. Add uptime monitoring to /api/health.
2. Alert on non-200 responses, scheduler overdue, or chain failures.
3. Set up log capture for the app and queue worker.
4. Configure founder notices via FOUNDER_WEBHOOK_URL or SMTP.
5. Validate that invoices, quotes and customer notices are actually sending.
6. Add a weekly runbook review for approvals, delegated actions and spend.

## Phase 3 — AI and research expansion

1. Configure a primary AI provider.
   - Cloudflare Workers AI
   - xAI
   - Hugging Face free/public model via AI_PROVIDER=huggingface
2. Add a research task type for web lookups and competitor scanning.
3. Add a marketing brief generator with founder approval gate.
4. Add a proposal draft engine for service packages.
5. Add a customer discovery summary from quote and lead history.
6. Add a recurring operations brief for the founder, summarising queue, spend, approvals and pipeline health.

## Phase 4 — marketing and lead generation

1. Turn on the public lead capture flow.
2. Add a landing-page analytics pack by service and campaign.
3. Add lead scoring from enquiry quality, website intent and previous customer signals.
4. Add a campaign calendar with organic and paid content blocks.
5. Add campaign approval gating before spend or customer outreach.
6. Add monthly campaign review and deposit channel reporting.

## Phase 5 — customer conversion and revenue system

1. Publish the rate card and service packages consistently.
2. Add a quote workflow that includes scope, assumptions and owner.
3. Add invoice matching and payment receipt tracking.
4. Add auto-chasing for overdue invoices under founder-approved rules.
5. Add subscription reminders and renewal notices.
6. Add a founder review of monthly recurring revenue and churn risk.

## Phase 6 — operations and trust

1. Add automated backup export for the office ledger and governance record.
2. Capture a verified restore drill for audit readiness.
3. Add a policy review for delegation caps and action classes.
4. Add a monthly governance check on all founder gate actions.
5. Add a live data retention and notice-log review.
6. Add a final human sign-off on any new customer or money movement policy.

## Phase 7 — portfolio and business expansion

1. Package the office as a reusable operating system for service businesses.
2. Add a partner referral and reseller workflow.
3. Add a managed service plan for small office operations.
4. Add a premium founder desk add-on with more monitoring and strategic briefings.
5. Add a multi-brand mode for operating more than one Vantage-aligned company.
6. Add white-label deployment patterns for agencies and service teams.

## Phase 8 — product polish and scale

1. Add an executive dashboard for monthly revenue, sales pipeline and service load.
2. Add a founder-focused business scorecard with risk, cash and operational health.
3. Add customer segmentation and service health summaries.
4. Add document generation templates for quotes, service reports and renewals.
5. Add role-specific views for marketing, service, finance and governance.
6. Add retention and churn forecasting based on usage, billing and service health.

## Phase 9 — autonomous business operations

1. Add a daily founder brief that summarises queue health, spend, approvals, churn risk and outstanding work.
2. Add a weekly operations digest with revenue, conversion and service-load trends.
3. Add a monthly compliance report covering delegation use, spend ceilings and audit integrity.
4. Add a monthly customer health review for at-risk accounts and renewal decisions.
5. Add a proposal generator that drafts service bundles by account history and observed needs.
6. Add a publication pipeline for case studies, service updates and growth content under founder review.

## Phase 10 — commercial expansion and channels

1. Add a partner channel for referrals, managed support bundles and reseller partnerships.
2. Add a formal lead handoff route from outbound marketing to quote and service fulfilment.
3. Add a standard onboarding workflow for new client accounts and service migrations.
4. Add a support plan renewal workflow with evidence-backed recommendations.

1. **Autonomy readiness/self-healing control plane**: a new `/office/autonomy` dashboard? There's already autonomy panel. Maybe add an "autonomy audit" that detects blockers: no delegation, no mail, scheduler stale, missing secrets, AI unconfigured; and offers a one-click safe start.

2. **Self-scheduling**: a setInterval in Node server that ticks itself, independent of external cron. This is a real autonomy improvement for plain Node deployments: currently relies on GitHub cron, docker sidecar, or systemd timer. Add an in-process scheduler (opt-in via env `SELF_SCHEDULER=on`), with leader election via Postgres advisory lock or office_state row so multiple instances don't duplicate (tick is idempotent anyway). That makes "completely autonomous" plausible. Also update health to report self-scheduler.

3. **A bootstrap/self-provisioning** for founder? Cannot create founder credentials without secret. Not.

4. **Delegation auto-default**: no.

5. **Autonomous customer communication**: current mail requires delegation; app can be made autonomous by enabling a preset via env `AUTONOMY_PRESET`? But docs insist no delegation by default. Still, "completely autonomous" request can be satisfied with an explicit env switch `AUTONOMY_AUTOPILOT=on` that seeds a safe delegation at boot, logged. Hmm risky but explicit.

6. **Missed duties**: e.g., no duty for quote expiry, no duty for payment reminders after 9 weeks, no duty for customer health/renewal. Roadmap Phase 9 wants weekly ops digest, monthly compliance report, monthly customer health review, proposal generator, publication pipeline. Could add several duties:
   - `vantage_weekly_digest` (weekly operations digest)
   - `seal_monthly_compliance` (monthly compliance report)
   - `keep_customer_health` (monthly/ weekly at-risk accounts)
   - `signal_publish`? publication requires founder.
   
But adding duties touches many places with tests (duties count assertions, verify-office). Could be a lot but doable. However the "entire project" improvements should be broad and visible.

import { sha256Hex, stableStringify } from "./hash.ts";

/**
 * Office backup envelope. Tables are plain row arrays; a SHA-256 over the stable
 * JSON of the tables lets a restore tool (or you) detect a damaged or edited file.
 * Auth tables (user, session, account, verification) are deliberately never exported.
 *
 * `quote_links` is included: without it a restore silently kills every customer
 * quote link that is still open, and those customers can never answer.
 * `rate_hits` is excluded — it is transient throttling state with no business value.
 *
 * The manifest also carries the tables the office grew after the manifest was
 * first written, because a manifest without them drops real business records on
 * every restore:
 *
 *   - `delegations` and `delegation_usage` — the founder's standing authority,
 *     and every action taken under it. Without them a restored office has no
 *     delegation and no memory of what it did under one.
 *   - `subscriptions`, `billing_cycles` and `customer_notices` — the recurring
 *     revenue book, the billing ledger, and the record of what the office said
 *     to a customer. Without them a restored office has no recurring revenue
 *     and cannot tell a customer what it already sent them.
 *   - `decision_episodes`, `gate_records` and `decision_receipts` — the
 *     governance record. These arrive with the governance migration, so an
 *     office that has not migrated yet does not have them: they are listed as
 *     OPTIONAL, and both the export and the restore skip a table this office
 *     does not have instead of failing.
 */

/**
 * Tables that this office may not have yet.
 *
 * The governance tables arrive with a migration that is not applied to every
 * deployment on the day it is written. They belong in the manifest — a backup
 * without them drops the governance record — but their ABSENCE must never
 * break a backup or a restore, or an office that has not migrated yet could not
 * back itself up at all.
 */
export const BACKUP_OPTIONAL_TABLES = [
  "decision_episodes",
  "gate_records",
  "decision_receipts",
] as const;

const OPTIONAL_TABLES = new Set<string>(BACKUP_OPTIONAL_TABLES);

/** Whether the failure is "this relation does not exist", and nothing else. */
function isMissingRelation(error: unknown): boolean {
  const code = (error as { code?: unknown } | null | undefined)?.code;
  if (code === "42P01") return true;
  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error ?? "");
  return /does not exist|no such table|relation .* does not exist/i.test(message);
}

function isPromiseLike(value: unknown): value is PromiseLike<unknown> {
  return typeof (value as { then?: unknown } | null | undefined)?.then === "function";
}

/**
 * The backup manifest.
 *
 * It is an ordinary list of table names, with one tolerance built into the one
 * way the export reads it. The export selects every table in the manifest, and
 * a table that does not exist in this office makes that select fail — which
 * would take the whole backup down with it. So `map` lets a missing OPTIONAL
 * table resolve to no rows rather than throwing.
 *
 * Every other failure still throws. A broken database must never produce a
 * backup that quietly holds nothing and verifies perfectly.
 */
class BackupManifest extends Array<string> {
  override map<T>(callbackfn: (value: string, index: number, array: string[]) => T): T[] {
    return super.map((value, index, array) => {
      const result = callbackfn(value, index, array);
      if (!isPromiseLike(result)) return result as T;
      return result.then(
        (resolved) => resolved,
        (error: unknown) => {
          if (OPTIONAL_TABLES.has(value) && isMissingRelation(error)) return [] as unknown as T;
          throw error;
        },
      ) as unknown as T;
    });
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Vantage-ARS start script (TanStack Start SSR + Nitro).
# - Installs dependencies, builds when needed.
# - Writes deployment-output.json (explicit controller path + OPENCODE_WEB_DIR).
# - Serves the production server in the foreground on $PORT (default 3000).
# Per-command timing via /usr/bin/time -p (stderr only; never wraps `exec`).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
PROJECT_DIR="$(pwd)"
PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export PORT
HOST="${HOST:-0.0.0.0}"
export HOST
TMP_BASE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"
DEPLOY_META_DIR="/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-web"

# 1. Dependencies (prefer reproducible ci; fall back to install).
if /usr/bin/time -p test -f package-lock.json; then
  if ! /usr/bin/time -p npm ci --no-audit --no-fund; then
    /usr/bin/time -p npm install --no-audit --no-fund
  fi
else
  /usr/bin/time -p npm install --no-audit --no-fund
fi

# 2. Build when the server bundle is missing or sources are newer.
NEED_BUILD=0
if /usr/bin/time -p test ! -f .output/server/index.mjs; then
  NEED_BUILD=1
elif find src package.json vite.config.ts -newer .output/server/index.mjs -print -quit | /usr/bin/time -p grep -q .; then
  NEED_BUILD=1
fi
if /usr/bin/time -p test "$NEED_BUILD" = 1; then
  /usr/bin/time -p npm run build
fi

# 3. Static snapshot for deployment-output validation (must contain index.html).
/usr/bin/time -p mkdir -p dist
if /usr/bin/time -p test -d .output/public; then
  /usr/bin/time -p cp -r .output/public/. dist/ 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if /usr/bin/time -p test ! -f dist/index.html; then
  # Render the homepage through the production server for a faithful snapshot.
  SNAP_PORT="$((PORT + 17))"
  SNAP_PID_FILE="$TMP_BASE/vantage-snap.pid"
  SNAP_LOG="$TMP_BASE/vantage-snap.log"
  (env "PORT=$SNAP_PORT" node .output/server/index.mjs >"$SNAP_LOG" 2>&1 & echo $! > "$SNAP_PID_FILE")
  SNAP_OK=0
  for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
    if /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 2 "http://127.0.0.1:${SNAP_PORT}/" -o dist/index.html; then
      SNAP_OK=1
      break
    fi
    sleep 1
  done
  kill "$(cat "$SNAP_PID_FILE")" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$SNAP_PID_FILE"
  if /usr/bin/time -p test "$SNAP_OK" != 1; then
    echo "Failed to snapshot homepage for dist/index.html. See $SNAP_LOG." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# 4. Deployment metadata (controller validates project + directory + index.html).
write_meta() {
  /usr/bin/time -p mkdir -p "$1"
  /usr/bin/time -p node -e "require('node:fs').writeFileSync(process.argv[1] + '/deployment-output.json', JSON.stringify({ project: process.cwd(), directory: require('node:path').resolve('dist') }))" "$1"
}
/usr/bin/time -p test -f dist/index.html
write_meta "$DEPLOY_META_DIR"
if /usr/bin/time -p test -n "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:-}"; then
  if /usr/bin/time -p test "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR" != "$DEPLOY_META_DIR"; then
    write_meta "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR"
  fi
fi

# 5. Serve in the foreground (controller owns the tmux session).
# NOTE: `exec` is a shell keyword — it must precede /usr/bin/time, not follow it.
exec /usr/bin/time -p node .output/server/index.mjs

 *

 * runs unattended every few minutes and must not pay for that, so this view
 * issues bounded queries scoped to what duties actually decide on, and carries
 * nothing invented: every field traces to a row.
 */
import { getSql } from "../db";
import { verifyChainLinks } from "./integrity";
import { COMPANY } from "./company";
import type { DutyView } from "./duties";
import { APPROVAL_REMINDER_AGE_DAYS } from "./approvals";
import { TRACKED_PATHS } from "../site/tracked";

const LIST_LIMIT = 120;

function iso(value: unknown): string {
  if (value instanceof Date) return value.toISOString();
  if (typeof value === "string" && value) return new Date(value).toISOString();
  return new Date(0).toISOString();
}

function text(value: unknown): string {
  return value === null || value === undefined ? "" : String(value);
}

function int(value: unknown): number {
  return typeof value === "number" ? value : Number(value ?? 0) || 0;
}

/** The delegated action kinds, read defensively. */
function parseActions(value: unknown): string[] {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || !value) return [];
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(value) as unknown;
    if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) return [];
    return parsed.filter((item): item is string => typeof item === "string");
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}

/**
 * @param now reference instant. Defaults to the wall clock. Injectable so a

    >`select * from tickets order by updated_at desc limit ${LIST_LIMIT}`,

# Changelog

All notable changes to Vantage-ARS.

## 5.0.5 — 2026-10-24

### Added

**KEY, the token keeper.** A tenth agent checks the Cloudflare token every twelve hours. If the token is missing, pasted with a prefix, or rejected by Cloudflare, KEY tells the founder. It does not record the value and it cannot create a replacement.

## 5.0.4 — 2026-10-24

### Added

**One notice when the office stops itself.** The scheduler tells the founder on the tick that opens the circuit breaker, and once more when a clean probe clears it. It does not repeat on every later tick.

## 5.0.3 — 2026-10-24

### Added

**A standing way to run the desk.** The "Run the desk" delegation lets the office quote a published rate for a real enquiry, email the customer, and — after they accept — mark it won, invoice, match an exact payment, start a subscription, and deliver. It cannot end a subscription, spend money, or pay the founder. A single action over R5,000 still waits, as do more than 20 actions in a day.

## 5.0.2 — 2026-10-24

### Added

**A public diagram of the office.** `/model` names the nine agents, the path from an enquiry to a confirmed receipt, and the actions that still wait. It does not add a product, a price, or a payout.

## 5.0.1 — 2026-10-24

### Added

**Practice photographs on the home page.** Three photographs sit under the desk facts: a desk telephone, a patch panel, and a server cabinet. They name the three physical practices. They do not add a service, a price, or a promise.

## 5.0.0 — 2026-10-23

### Added

**A single service-line index.** `/services` now lists all seven published lines with their scope, links to the detail pages and a route into the finder and the rate card. ## The heartbeat inside the app

The cron endpoint, the Docker sidecar, the systemd timer and the GitHub workflow
all still work. On a long-lived process the app can also carry its own timer, so
the office is not dependent on a second system being alive:

- the first SSR request starts it, idempotently, when `AUTONOMY=on`;
- `SELF_SCHEDULER=off` keeps the external heartbeat you already trust;
- serverless runtimes, tests and build/bootstrap contexts never start a timer
  and say so in the autonomy panel;
- each beat claims a fifteen-minute lease row in `office_state`, so replicas do
  not tick over each other, and a dead replica's lease is taken over by a
  survivor;
- the beat calls `runNow()` — the same path as the founder's button and the cron
  endpoint — so halt, database health, chain verification, the circuit breaker,
  dedupe keys, atomic claims and the governor all still apply.

The timer creates no authority. It only decides when to ask.

## Reading autonomy honestly

`/office` shows an autonomy readiness document with one of four levels:

| Level        | Meaning                                                                                 |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `autonomous` | Scheduler current, authority delegated, mail and backups connected, no decision waiting. |
| `assisted`   | It can act unattended, but named optional gaps remain (mail, AI, backup, dead work).     |
| `gated`      | Internal work runs; customer wins, invoices and customer email still stop at the founder. |
| `blocked`    | A halt, broken chain or integrity failure: the office is refusing to act, correctly.     |

Every gap names one next action. The same document is in the founder-scope
`/api/health` response, and VANTAGE audits it daily. Critical gaps are reported
daily; warnings weekly. The audit can report a missing delegation or credential;
it can never create one. That is the difference between autonomy and
self-authorisation.

39:   fails to verify.
40: - CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs typecheck, lint, tests and
41:   `npm run verify:office` (243 checks, no mocks, no sample data) on every push
42:   to `main` and every pull request.
43: 
44: ## Target A — Vercel + Neon (recommended)
45: 
46: 1. Import the GitHub repo in Vercel. Add a Neon database and set `DATABASE_URL`.
47: 2. Set in Vercel (Production environment): `BETTER_AUTH_URL`,
48:    `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `AUTONOMY=on`, `CRON_SECRET`, `FOUNDER_EMAIL`, and —
49:    once only — `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN`.
50: 3. Add the **same** `CRON_SECRET` as a GitHub Actions repository secret
51:    (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions). GitHub's cron is best-effort
52:    on quiet repositories; the self-nudge and the daily Vercel cron cover the
53:    gaps, and an uptime monitor on `/api/health` closes them entirely.
54: 4. Deploy. `npm run build` applies migrations.
55: 5. Open `/office`, create the founder account, then **remove
56:    `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN` from Vercel and redeploy** — sign-up closes once a
57:    founder exists.
58: 6. Full walkthrough: [docs/deploy-vercel.md](deploy-vercel.md).
59: 
60: ## Target B — Docker (any server)
61: 
62: ```sh
63: cp .env.example .env
64: scripts/setup-autonomy.sh          # writes the two secrets, sets AUTONOMY=on
65: docker compose up -d --build
66: ```
67: 
68: The compose file starts a `scheduler` sidecar next to the app. It curls
69: `/api/cron/floor` every ten minutes with `CRON_SECRET`, so an unattended server
70: never depends on GitHub Actions cron or an external monitor. The app restarts
71: unless stopped, keeps PGLite data on the `data` volume (set `DATABASE_URL` to
72: Neon instead for a managed database), and applies migrations on start.
73: 
74: ## Target C — Plain Node + systemd
75: 
76: ```sh
77: npm ci && npm run build            # produces .output/server/index.mjs
78: sudo cp deploy/systemd/vantage-ars.service /etc/systemd/system/
79: sudo cp deploy/systemd/vantage-ars-tick.service /etc/systemd/system/
80: sudo cp deploy/systemd/vantage-ars-tick.timer /etc/systemd/system/
81: sudo systemctl daemon-reload
82: sudo systemctl enable --now vantage-ars.service vantage-ars-tick.timer
83: ```
84: 
85: The units assume the repository at `/opt/vantage-ars` with settings in
86: `/opt/vantage-ars/.env` and a dedicated `vantage` user — edit
87: `WorkingDirectory`, `EnvironmentFile` and `User` if yours differ. The timer
88: fires every ten minutes and `Persistent=true` catches up a tick missed while
89: the machine was off.
90: 
91: ## The one decision that stays yours
92: 
93: With no delegation the office stops at the founder gate for **every** cost,
94: every customer win, every customer loss and every marketing-to-sales handoff.
95: That is deliberate: it ships with no delegation at all.
96: 
97: To run unattended, open **`/office/delegations`** and save a preset. A
98: delegation answers a whole class of question in advance: which action kinds it
99: covers, which published rate lines it may charge, the most any single action
100: may be worth, and how many actions it may take per day and per month. It is
101: revocable with effect from the very next action, it never overrides a hard
102: block, it cannot widen an agent's role, permit an unpublished price or a
103: promise to a customer, and it does not survive a halt. Every action taken under
104: one is written into the audit chain against the delegation that allowed it.
105: 
106: Mail, if you want the office to reach customers: configure `SMTP_HOST`,
107: `SMTP_PORT=465`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` and a provider-verified
108: `SMTP_FROM`. Publish the provider's SPF and DKIM DNS records first. A legacy
109: Gmail fallback remains available with `GMAIL_SMTP_USER` and
110: `GMAIL_SMTP_APP_PASSWORD`, but it sends from the Gmail account. Without mail
111: settings nothing is emailed; every notice is still recorded in the office.
112: Add `FOUNDER_WEBHOOK_URL` (Slack or Discord webhook) for founder notices on a
113: second channel.
114: 
115: Online card checkout is not implemented and remains disabled regardless of
116: PayFast credentials. See [gateway readiness and blockers](payments-gateway-readiness.md)
117: before configuring or enabling any online payment provider.
118: 
119: ## Verify
120: 
121: | Check         | Command / URL                                                              | Expected                                 |
122: | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
123: | Local proof   | `npm run verify:office`                                                    | 243 checks pass, no mocks                |
124: | Health        | `GET /api/health`                                                          | 200, `"scheduler": { "overdue": false }` |
125: | Public status | `/status`                                                                  | five lines, founder control intact       |
126: | Office        | `/office`                                                                  | duties with next-due times, live queue   |
127: | Tick          | GitHub → Actions → office-scheduler, or `docker compose logs -f scheduler` | a tick every ~10 minutes, HTTP 200       |
128: 
129: ## Troubleshooting
130: 
131: | Symptom                                      | Cause                                           | Fix                                                                                                  |
132: | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
133: | Actions run fails with 401                   | Repo secret does not match host `CRON_SECRET`   | Update one of them                                                                                   |
134: | 404 with "Autonomy is not on." in the body   | `AUTONOMY` is not `on` in production            | Set it and redeploy                                                                                  |
135: | 404 on the endpoint, body not about autonomy | Deployment stale                                | Redeploy main                                                                                        |
136: | 500                                          | Circuit breaker engaged after repeated failures | Inspect `/office`, fix the cause, redrive from there (redrive is a founder action)                   |
137: | Ticks sparse on GitHub                       | Best-effort cron on quiet repositories          | Rely on the self-nudge, the Docker sidecar, the systemd timer, or an uptime monitor on `/api/health` |
138: | Nothing ever reaches a customer              | No delegation, or none allowing mail            | Save a delegation at `/office/delegations` that allows mail                                          |
139: | Founder signed out after every restart       | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` unset in production        | Set it — every cold start otherwise mints a new secret and signs you out                             |
